extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and attorneys using Public PAIR
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading and interpreting prosecution documents and Office actions available in USPTO Public PAIR, including meanings of common document types, forms, and statutory rejections. Useful for practitioners checking file history and responding to examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content ordering in Public PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: The content entries are in reverse chronological order and the same type of action may appear over the course of prosecution until the application is ultimately either patented or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing the file, expect newer documents first; the same document type (e.g., Office action) can appear multiple times at different prosecution stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: (CTFR) Final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any second or any subsequent Office action (may include grounds of objections, rejections, and/or other requirements) from the examiner that is made final indicating that the examiner intends to close prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a final rejection, applicant no longer has the right to amend the application unless the amendment merely cancels claims or complies with a formal requirement made earlier. Use this to determine whether prosecution is being closed and what types of amendments remain available.

rubrics_metrics.name: (A...) Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment filed by the applicant in response to an Office action issued by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply to an Office action may or may not include an amendment to the claims and/or written description. Look for amendments attached to replies to see claim or specification changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: (CLM) Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for the most recent copy of claims to see if any amendments have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always refer to the latest claims document in the file to determine current claim language and scope; claim status may change over multiple Office actions and replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: (REM) Remarks (applicant's reply arguments)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the arguments/remarks portion of applicant’s reply to an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant’s reply must distinctly and specifically point out the supposed errors in the examiner's action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action in order to entitle applicant to reconsideration or further examination. The arguments/remarks must point out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims, including any newly presented claims, patentable over any applied references. Use REM to assess the applicant's legal and factual responses and whether they preserve rights to further examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: (CTNF) Non-final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an Office action by the examiner which does not close prosecution of the application (compared to a final Office action which intends to close prosecution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office action may include requirements, objections, and/or rejections. Non-final rejections permit amendments and further responses; track whether issues are open for amendment/clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: (892) Form PTO-892 (examiner-cited references)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner provides Form 892 as an attachment to any Office action in which the examiner cites references not previously of record in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form 892 to identify newly cited prior art that the examiner relied upon. It signals references that the applicant may need to address in a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: (SRFW) File Wrapper Search Info
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional search information relating to the examiner’s field of search including classification, databases and other areas searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRFW gives context on where the examiner looked and may help assess the thoroughness and scope of the examiner's search.

rubrics_metrics.name: (SRNT) Search Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: These are notes on searches performed by the examiner during the examination of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches may include database search results, internet search results, non-patent literature searches and searches of U.S. and foreign patent documents. Use SRNT to understand search strategies and what materials the examiner considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: (1449) Form PTO-1449 (applicant-known references)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant provides Form 1449 identifying references known to the applicant to be material to the patentability of the claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant complies with the requirements of the rules and the examiner considers the references listed on the form 1449, the examiner will initial the form and a copy is attached with the Office action. This documents applicant-disclosed prior art and the examiner's acknowledgement of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 101 rejections (subject matter/utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections made under 35 U.S.C. § 101 are based on non-statutory subject matter or lack of utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-statutory subject matter includes abstract ideas, laws of nature, and natural phenomena. A lack of utility under § 101 is similar to a lack of Industrial Applicability (IA) in an international application. Use §101 entries to determine if the examiner finds the claimed subject matter outside patent-eligible categories or lacking practical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 102 rejections (novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections made under 35 U.S.C. § 102 are based on a lack of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference applied in a § 102 rejection is similar to a “X” category reference in a search report of an international application. Use §102 to identify applied single-reference anticipations (novelty issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections made under 35 U.S.C. § 103 are based on obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The references applied in the § 103 rejection are similar to “Y” category references for lack of inventive step in a search report of an international application. §103 entries indicate examiner's combined-reference obviousness reasoning that applicant must rebut or overcome.
